field: *** THE ENTRY ITSELF, NINE DAYS AFTER THE INDEX FOUND IT ***
value: STANDESAMT SCHÖNEBERG II, HEIRATSREGISTER 1924, NR. 6. Landesarchiv Berlin, P Rep. 161 Nr. 171. Two sheets scanned and sent by Arabella Oberle, Landesarchiv Berlin, 29 September 2026. The Namensverzeichnis that found it on 20 September is P Rep. 161 Nr. 271 — A DIFFERENT VOLUME. Index and register are not the same shelfmark and this archive had only ever cited the index.

field: the marriage
value: Berlin-Schöneberg, am FÜNFTEN JANUAR TAUSEND NEUNHUNDERT VIER UND ZWANZIG — 5 JANUARY 1924. Aufgebotsverzeichnis Nr. 11.. (the last figures are not legible in this scan).

field: 1. the groom
value: der KAUFMANN JAKOB LEIBHOLZ, der Persönlichkeit nach auf Grund der Aufgebotsverhandlung anerkannt, geboren am ACHTEN AUGUST des Jahres tausend acht hundert VIER UND ACHTZIG zu SCHUBIN, Geburtsregister Nr. — des Standesamts in SCHUBIN, wohnhaft in BERLIN-SCHÖNEBERG, FREISINGER STRASSE 19.

field: and his birth date agrees with the Schubin register to the day
value: the birth entry read at the image on 22 September — Standesamt Schubin, Geburtsregister 1884, AKT NR. 63 — gives 8 AUGUST 1884. The Berlin clerk of 1924 wrote the same day from the papers in front of him. TWO REGISTERS IN TWO COUNTRIES, FORTY YEARS AND SIX HUNDRED KILOMETRES APART, AGREEING WITHOUT EITHER KNOWING THE OTHER. Note the register NUMBER is left as a dash here; this archive supplies it, and the archive of Bydgoszcz supplied it first.

field: 2. the bride
value: die MODISTIN AUGUSTE LUWINSKI, der Persönlichkeit nach auf Grund der Aufgebotsverhandlung anerkannt, geboren am ACHT UND ZWANZIGSTEN AUGUST des Jahres tausend acht hundert DREI UND NEUNZIG zu SAUERBAUM KREIS RÖSSEL, GEBURTSREGISTER NR. 88 DES STANDESAMTS IN GROSS-BÖSSAU, wohnhaft in BERLIN-SCHÖNEBERG, INNSBRUCKER STRASSE 39.

field: *** AND THAT CITATION IS THE MOST USEFUL LINE ON THE PAGE ***
value: AUGUSTE'S BIRTH ENTRY HAS A NUMBER AND AN OFFICE: GROSS-BÖSSAU, 1893, NR. 88. This archive has swept the Ermland for Luwinskis for weeks with nothing but a village name. A birth entry names the parents, so JOACHIM LUWINSKI and JOHANNA née THIMM — two of the four names the archive has never seen on a document — are now one ordered copy away, from a register office this archive had not previously known to ask.

field: *** THE READING THE CLERK SETTLED HIMSELF ***
value: the groom's house number is one glyph and it was NOT obvious. IT IS SETTLED BY THIS CLERK'S OWN HAND ELSEWHERE ON HIS OWN PAGE: his 4, in "46 Jahre alt" for the first witness, is ANGULAR, OPEN-TOPPED AND SITS ON THE BASELINE WITH NO DESCENDER; his 9, in "Innsbrucker Straße 39" three lines below, has A CLOSED ROUND BOWL AND A DESCENDER. The disputed glyph has the bowl and the descender. IT IS A 9. Not reasoned from the alphabet — matched against the same man writing the same figure where the answer is already known.

field: and all three Schöneberg addresses are the same quarter
value: FREISINGER STRASSE (groom, 1924) · INNSBRUCKER STRASSE (bride, 1924) · MERANER STRASSE (the household, 1939 census). ALL THREE ARE IN THE BAYERISCHES VIERTEL. They were living separately, a few streets apart, in the same corner of Schöneberg, fifteen years before the census put them under one roof in it.

field: 3. the first witness
value: der KAUFMANN SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ, der Persönlichkeit nach auf Grund SEINER LEGITIMATIONSKARTE anerkannt, 46 JAHRE ALT, wohnhaft in BERLIN, BELLEALLIANCEPLATZ 6.

field: *** WHICH IS THE FIRST DOCUMENT PUTTING SAMUEL BESIDE JACOB ***
value: this archive has followed Samuel Leibholz for weeks through directories and telephone books — the wholesale hat business, SW19 to SW68, the forename replaced by the imposed one in 1940 — and has always called him Jacob's brother on the strength of a shared surname and a shared Schubin. HERE HE IS, STANDING AT JACOB'S WEDDING. 46 in January 1924 puts his birth in 1877 or 1878, which is what this archive already carried. A witness need not be a brother and this does not prove he was one; IT IS THE FIRST TIME THE TWO MEN APPEAR ON ONE PIECE OF PAPER.

field: and it is an address twelve years earlier than any the archive held
value: BELLEALLIANCEPLATZ 6 in 1924 — today Mehringplatz, in Kreuzberg. The directory run had him at SW19 from 1929 and SW68 from 1938. THIS IS NEW AND IT IS THE EARLIEST.

field: 4. the second witness
value: der KAUFMANN WALTER WOTTRICH, der Persönlichkeit nach auf Grund DER GEBURTSURKUNDE anerkannt, 26 JAHRE ALT, wohnhaft in BERLIN-LICHTENBERG, SIMONSTRASSE 18. A NAME ENTIRELY NEW TO THIS ARCHIVE. Identified by his birth certificate rather than a Legitimationskarte, which is what a young man without papers of standing would produce. The street is read as Simonstraße and the reading is not certain.

field: the four signatures
value: JAKOB LEIBHOLZ · AUGUSTE LEIBHOLZ GEBORENE LUWINSKI · SAMUEL LEIBHOLZ · WALTER WOTTRICH. Auguste signs in her new name with her old one after it, in her own hand.

field: *** MARGIN ONE — 5 JUNE 1939 ***
value: Auf Grund der Zweiten Verordnung vom 17. August 1938 zur Durchführung des Gesetzes über die Änderung von Familiennamen und Vornamen führt der nebenbezeichnete Ehemann zusätzlich den Vornamen: ISRAEL. THE LAW REACHING BACK FIFTEEN YEARS INTO A CLOSED REGISTER TO ADD A NAME TO A MAN'S WEDDING.

field: *** MARGIN TWO — 4 APRIL 1940, AND IT ANSWERS A QUESTION THIS ARCHIVE REFUSED TO GUESS ***
value: Durch das am 21. MÄRZ 1940 rechtskräftig gewordene Urteil des LANDGERICHTS BERLIN 251. R. 80. 40 ist die Ehe zwischen dem JAKOB LEIBHOLZ und der AUGUSTE LEIBHOLZ GEBORENE LUWINSKI GESCHIEDEN WORDEN. THE MARRIAGE WAS DIVORCED.

field: and at the foot of the second sheet
value: Zu 1. 'Zum 2. Male geh. Nr. 2476/1940 — party 1 is Jakob. HE MARRIED A SECOND TIME IN 1940, entry number 2476 of that year. The office name after it is blotted and is not read here.

field: what the divorce does to the 1940 directory puzzle
value: the 1940 Berliner Adressbuch has "LEIBHOLZ AUGUSTE, WITWE, Schöneberg, Badensche Str 9". This archive set out three possibilities — an error, a different woman, or something that happened to the marriage before 1940 that it did not know about — AND REFUSED TO PICK ONE. THE THIRD IS NOW DOCUMENTED. The marriage ended by judgment in March 1940 and Jacob lived until 1943, so the entry is no longer in flat contradiction with anything.

field: AND IT IS STILL NOT SOLVED, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT SENTENCE
value: A DIVORCED WOMAN IS NOT A WIDOW. "Witwe" remains wrong on its own terms, and the 1940 volume was compiled from returns gathered BEFORE the decree became final on 21 March 1940 — so "she was divorced, hence the directory said widow" does not work as an explanation either. What has gone is the contradiction that made the identification impossible. What has not gone is the word.

field: and it dates a marriage the archive has been hunting
value: AUGUSTE "LIZZY" LUWINSKI DIED AT KRAICHTAL IN 1975 AS AUGUSTE FRICKE. The Fricke marriage has never been found. IT NOW HAS A FLOOR: it cannot be earlier than 21 MARCH 1940. Forty post-war volumes have been swept for her under that name; the sweep now has a date to work from.

field: *** AND ONE PREDICTION OF THIS ARCHIVE'S IS SIMPLY WRONG ***
value: on 20 September, before the entry was seen, this archive wrote that it would name "BOTH SETS OF PARENTS — for Auguste JOACHIM LUWINSKI and JOHANNA née THIMM, and for Jacob SALLY LEIBHOLZ and FRIEDERIKE née SCHMUL. Four names this archive believes it knows and has never seen confirmed on one document." IT NAMES NO PARENTS AT ALL. The Prussian marriage entry of the 1920s cites each party's BIRTH REGISTER instead of naming their parents. The four names are still unconfirmed on one document, and the entry instead hands over the two citations that lead to the documents which do name them.

field: *** AND THE OTHER PREDICTION IS A NEGATIVE, WHICH IS ALSO AN ANSWER ***
value: the same note said: "if Kurt Luwinski, born 11 May 1912 and twelve years old at this wedding, was legitimised by his mother's marriage, THE NOTE IS IN THE MARGIN OF THIS ENTRY." THERE IS NO SUCH NOTE. The margin carries the 1939 name decree and the 1940 divorce and nothing else. KURT WAS NOT LEGITIMISED BY THIS MARRIAGE, which is consistent with everything else about him: he carried LUWINSKI out of Germany in 1933 and to his death in Johannesburg in 1968.

field: source
